title: The keys, 1921
hook: the Sikhs won back the keys of the Golden Temple treasury by peaceful protest

segments.voice: Yesterday, Nankana, and your line was they did not strike back. Did you let one chance to hit back pass? Today, the same refusal, and this time it wins something. Day nine hundred eighty-six.

A bunch of keys on a ring. They open the toshakhana, the treasury of the Golden Temple, where its precious gifts and offerings are kept. In late 1921, just as the new Sikh committee asks for them, an official acting for the British government takes them into the government's hands. On paper it's a small administrative step. To Sikhs, it's a message: you may pray here, but we still hold the keys. What happens next turns a bunch of keys into a national story. Today: the keys.
screen: `A BUNCH OF KEYS.` → `THE TEMPLE'S TREASURY.` → `TAKEN BY THE GOVERNMENT.`

segments.voice: First, what the keys meant. The new committee, the SGPC, had begun to manage the Golden Temple. Taking the treasury keys back into government hands said that the British, not the Sangat, still had the last word. Second, the protest. Sikhs answered with meetings, speeches and refusals, all of them peaceful. Leaders were arrested, including Baba Kharak Singh, a respected head of the committee. More volunteers stepped forward and were arrested in their turn. The protest stayed peaceful. Third, the giving way. The protest spread, and the arrests didn't stop it. In the end the government backed down. The prisoners were released, and the keys were handed to Baba Kharak Singh. Accounts say Mahatma Gandhi sent a telegram of congratulation, calling it the first decisive battle for India's freedom won. Fourth, the deeper key. In a salok at Ang 1237 of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Guru is called the key: the mind is a locked room, and only the Guru's key opens it. That verse is about the inner life, not a treasury. But it points at what Sikhs remember about this protest. In their telling, the keys in the government's keeping were never the real power; the Sangat's discipline was. Without striking anyone, the community had won back what was theirs. Gandhi's telegram called it a first battle won, and more were coming. That's today's line.
screen: `WHO HOLDS THE KEYS?` · `MEETINGS, ARRESTS, NO VIOLENCE.` · `THE KEYS HANDED BACK.` · `THE GURU IS THE KEY.` · then, large: `FIRST BATTLE WON.`

segments.voice: Two minutes for a peaceful resolve. Sit, and let your breath slow. If you have a key nearby, hold it in your palm and feel its weight. If not, picture one. Think of something you're working toward that won't come quickly: a change at work, a repair in a family, a habit you're breaking. Breathe in, and feel the key. Breathe out, and decide, quietly, to keep going without forcing it and without giving up. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
The keys. The keys of the Golden Temple treasury, taken into government hands and won back by the Sikhs through peaceful protest. Today's word.
Your line: first battle won. Today, take one patient, peaceful step toward the thing you're working on, and count it as a win. Day nine hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Sikhs remember the keys affair, the Chabian da Morcha, as an early victory of the gurdwara reform movement, won by peaceful protest; the toshakhana of the Golden Temple is still kept under the SGPC's management.

give up and let the government keep them.

original.note: kunji, key; in Gurbani the Guru is the key to the locked mind.

what it means: a peaceful protest that won back the Golden Temple's treasury keys from the British.
what a scholar hears: accounts say Gandhi called it the first decisive battle for India's freedom won; it set the pattern of the protests that followed.

notes: The carry 'first battle won' echoes the telegram attributed to Gandhi ('First decisive battle for India's freedom won'); the voice gives it as 'accounts say' and paraphrases. Please confirm the wording and source before any quotation.
The handover of the keys took place in early 1922 by most accounts; the script avoids the date, since the index title says 1921. A Keeper may wish to adjust the title.
Baba Kharak Singh's role and arrest, and the release of prisoners: confirm.
Ang 1237 (Sarang ki Var, salok M2, the Guru as key) paraphrased; please confirm the Ang and the attribution to Guru Angad.
'Nobody stormed the treasury. Nobody struck an official.' is a strong claim; please confirm or soften.
The name Chabian da Morcha and the present SGPC management of the toshakhana in howItsDone: confirm.

Editor: cut the invented 'iron, heavy' detail; 'Nobody stormed the treasury. Nobody struck an official.' softened to 'the protest stayed peaceful'; the narrator's 'it was the first battle' now attributed to Gandhi's telegram and to Sikh memory; 'your holiest treasury' (superlative) in the fork replaced.

Audit: the keys were taken from the government-appointed manager (sarbrah) by an official acting for the Deputy Commissioner (accounts name Lala Amar Nath), not 'a British official' taking them 'from the Sikh committee'; hook, screen, word, match, fork and teach corrected. Confirm.
